description: I am a student at Universidad Privada de Trujillo (UPRIT), focused on learning and applying Python and web architectures to solve critical planetary challenges. I chose the challenge 'Shift the Routine: Adapting Farms with NASA Data,' designing an intelligent decision-support tool to mitigate water scarcity, optimize agricultural resources, and promote climate resilience locally and globally.
summary: Órbita Moche is a web-based water resilience and smart crop rotation platform designed for critical tail-end agricultural zones of the Tinajones system, primarily Mórrope and San José in Peru. The platform translates open NASA datasets (NASA POWER, SMAP, GPM, and Landsat/SRDTM) into actionable early irrigation alerts, protecting vulnerable smallholders from over-pumping toxic brackish groundwater and severe soil salinization.
details: What it does & How it works: Órbita Moche provides a Flask-based web application featuring an interactive Leaflet map and a real-time agro-climate dashboard. It tracks soil moisture, precipitation, and thermal stress using NASA APIs to guide sustainable crop rotation and prevent saline groundwater extraction in Mórrope and San José. Tech Stack: Developed using Python, Flask, Gunicorn, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Leaflet.js, deployed via GitHub and Render. Creativity & Impact: It bridges high-resolution satellite Earth observation with the daily survival needs of small farmers facing extreme water scarcity at the edge of the Tinajones reservoir system.
